text:
incident-bot: Pager S2 — elevated error rate for canary pool 'eu-west-model-1' (since 2024-06-05 09:12 UTC). 503 and 429 tail spikes affecting ~7% of traffic. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/canary-failure. paging: @eng-oncall.
Alex P.: grabbing this. joining call in 2.
Mira G.: saw a redline on the latency dashboard, spikes correlate with requests hitting the redis-kv cache miss path.
Lee (ops): confirming, redis miss ratio + connection queue length jumped at 09:11. Topology: canary pods use new kernel + quant-runtime-2.
Sarah L.: is this across all canaries or just eu-west?
Mira G.: looks eu-west only, other regions normal.
Alex P.: initial hypothesis: new quant-runtime introduced a small increase in connection churn -> more cache misses -> higher downstream retries causing 503s.
Tasha C.: any customer impact? I see errors mostly for small percentage of PLG users (embed/short text). No known enterprise outage yet.
deploy-bot: Deploy 1723459001 started at 2024-06-05 08:59 UTC to eu-west, tag=quant-runtime-2, rollout=canary(10%).
Alex P.: ok plan: 1) divert traffic away from canary pool (route to stable) 2) flip canary feature flag off 3) if metrics back to normal, investigate kernel+runtime interaction offline.
Lee (ops): diverting now via routing control-plane. Command: ``/route update --pool eu-west-model-1 --weight 0.0 --to stable-model-1``
Alex P.: thanks. flipping feature flag: ``/ff toggle quant-runtime-2 --env eu-west --state off``
Mira G.: ping after flip — dashboards show 503 rate dropping instantly. tail-latency normalizing.
Tasha C.: noticed a handful of 429s still trickling, likely queued requests draining. Not seeing new 503s.
Alex P.: good. continuing to monitor 20m. creating a short incident note for SRE review.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-362. Severity S2. Link: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2024-362
Sarah L.: can we confirm rollback? I'm leaning to rollback to previous runtime build for canary while we root cause.
Alex P.: I'd prefer to hold off full rollback until canary traffic is stable; we've removed canary traffic and disabled flag which effectively stops the bad behavior. If after 30m metrics remain green we'll keep stable.
Lee (ops): adding a temporary circuit-breaker on redis client in eu-west for 10s to prevent retry floods: ``redis.client.cfg circuit_breaker=10s``
Mira G.: logs show a correlation between cache miss and a specific quantized kernel path. capturing trace logs to upload to the model-runtime team.
Tasha C.: notifying Customer Ops about limited PLG impact, will draft message in #support-ops. cc @Sarah L.
Alex P.: handoff planned at 10:00 UTC to night oncall if still stable. if error rate resurfaces, immediate rollback + pager escalation to S1.
Sarah L.: acknowleded. adding timeline + mitigation steps to the incident doc.
Mira G.: uploaded traces: https://redwood/logs/trace-1723459999, added pointer to PR that introduced quant runtime changes.
Alex P.: final check — 30m steady, 503 down from 7% to <0.1%, redis queue length normal. I'll close this thread and mark incident as mitigated but not resolved; follow-ups: postmortem, root-cause, canary config review.
Tasha C.: thanks team. I'll prepare customer-facing note if enterprise support asks. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-362 status updated to MITIGATED at 2024-06-05 10:02 UTC.
Alex P.: handing off to night oncall (Mira will stay 10m for handoff). Mira, please escalate immediately if any regression.
Mira G.: on it.
Lee (ops): closing routing change ticket in 30m if stable.``
